terms.section.account.body: You can delete your account on the Account page; you confirm it with your password. This removes your personal stock, favourites, private photos, profile picture, account links and sign-in access. It also removes a reported profile picture and every copy of it kept for a report (see “Your profile picture”). Shared glazes, combinations and public or club photos stay, shown without your name. Your shared text stays too, so remove identifying details before you delete your account. If you are a club's only member, the club is deleted as well, with its stock, invite link and club photos. A club with other members must keep an admin: if needed, make another member an admin first. After serious or repeated violations of these terms, the site admins may remove an account in the same way and block its email address from being used to register again. If a club would then be left without an admin, the member who has belonged to it longest becomes its admin. To recognise a blocked address, Glazelab keeps only a pseudonymous fingerprint of it, with the date and a short reason, for as long as the block stands. The fingerprint is calculated with a secret key, and the address cannot be read from it. No name is kept. Entries in the site admins' log of their actions (such as a ban, the account it removed and the reason) are deleted after 90 days. If you think your account was removed or your address blocked by mistake, or if you have questions about your account or these terms, contact the operator below. A block can be lifted.
terms.section.account.title: Your account and contact
terms.section.changes.body: These terms may be updated when the service changes. The version at the top shows which terms apply. Important changes will be announced in the app. If you do not agree with new terms, you can stop using the service and delete your account.
terms.section.changes.title: When these terms change
terms.section.conduct.body: Keep your account secure. Do not harass anyone, do not upload content that is not allowed, do not scrape the service and do not disrupt it. Misuse can get an account banned, and offending content may be removed.
terms.section.conduct.title: Play fair
terms.section.cookies.body: Glazelab sets only the cookies it needs to work. A sign-in cookie keeps you signed in. It stays valid for up to 30 days after you last used the service and for at most a year after you signed in. Your browser keeps it for up to a year, and it is removed when you sign out. Changing your password signs you out on all your other devices. A security cookie protects your actions against forged requests. It is set when you sign up, sign in or save something, and it lasts until you close the browser. There are no tracking, advertising or analytics cookies and no third-party cookies, and the app itself loads nothing from other websites. So that the app works offline and loads quickly, it also keeps some things on your device, in your browser's local storage, IndexedDB and cache: your settings (such as your language), a copy of your data and the photos it has loaded. Your browser keeps loaded photos for up to a week (public ones for up to a year). This copy stays on your device. Signing out or deleting your account removes the copy of your account. That includes the photos in your browser's cache where the browser supports this; browsers without that support keep them until they expire. Clearing the site data in your browser removes everything.
terms.section.cookies.title: Cookies and data on your device
terms.section.hobby.body: Glazelab is a hobby project for keeping notes on ceramic glazes, your stock and your tests. It is provided as available. There is no guarantee that it is always available, that everything in it is correct or that it suits a particular purpose, as far as the law allows. Rights and liability that the law does not allow anyone to exclude stay untouched.
terms.section.hobby.title: A hobby project
terms.section.hosting.body: All data of this Glazelab service is stored in the European Union, on a server that the operator runs privately at home. Your account details, notes and images are used only to run the service. Your account records which version of these terms you accepted and when.
terms.section.hosting.title: Where your data lives
terms.section.images.body: Upload only photos of your own ceramics, such as glaze tests and finished pieces. No one may be identifiable in them: no faces, no names, no other personal details. Your profile picture has its own rule below. Upload only what you own or have permission to share, and nothing unlawful or harmful.
terms.section.images.title: Your ceramic photos
terms.section.records.body: Keep your own copies of anything important. The service may change or stop, and data may be lost. Glaze notes and images are not safety advice: check firing conditions and food safety yourself before use.
terms.section.records.title: Keep your own copies
terms.section.sharing.body: Your content stays yours. You allow Glazelab to store, process and show it as far as needed to run the service, following the visibility you choose. This permission is not exclusive. Others can view and save public images, and copies may remain on their devices or in caches.
terms.section.sharing.title: Sharing your content
terms.section.buddies.body: You can become glaze buddies with other users. One of you asks, through a buddy link or a club's member list, and the other accepts. From then on, each of you sees the other's display name and which glazes the other has on their personal shelf. Buddies never see amounts, jar sizes, email addresses or club shelves. You can keep single glazes private, and you can end a buddy relationship at any time. Anyone who has your buddy link sees your display name and can ask to be your buddy, until you replace the link. Buddy requests and relationships are deleted with your account.

about.title: About Glazelab
about.lead: Glazelab is a place to manage your ceramic glazes, your shelf and your clubs, and to record and explore glaze combinations. It is privacy friendly, and you can host it yourself if you want.
about.origin.title: Where it comes from
about.origin.body: Glazelab began as a replacement for the shared documents and spreadsheets where potters kept their glaze notes and combinations. They were hard to browse and hard to search. Here you can explore combinations by their photos, search by text or glaze, and narrow the list with tags, the firing and quick views such as “I can make now”.
about.lab.title: An experimental lab for your glazes
about.lab.body: Record each combination as the steps you took: the glazes, the coats, how they went on and the final firing. Add photos of test tiles and finished pieces, keep a draft to yourself until it is ready, and record a variation when you want to change one thing. Your shelf knows which glazes you have, so you can see what you could make today.
about.inspiration.title: Inspiration, not social media
about.inspiration.body: Explore what other potters have tried and take their ideas further with a variation of your own. There are no comments and no followers: just creative freedom, without pressure. You can star glazes and combinations to find them again. Explore can sort by how often something was starred, but nobody sees who starred it.
about.inspiration.people: A club shares a shelf and its members' combinations, and glaze buddies see which glazes are on your shelf. You decide who you share with: clubs take new members only through an invite link, and both buddies have to agree.
about.privacy.title: Privacy friendly
about.privacy.body: There is no advertising and no tracking. Glazelab sets only the cookies it needs to work, and the app loads nothing from other websites. Error reports are off unless you turn them on. Barcodes and jar labels are read on your device, and uploaded photos lose their location and camera data. The terms of service say what is kept and for how long.
about.open.title: Open source, and yours to host
about.open.body: Glazelab is open source under the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3 or later. You can run your own copy: the instructions are with the source code. Whoever runs a copy decides where its data lives, and its terms of service say where.
about.free.title: Free forever
about.free.body: Free to use, and meant to stay that way. There is no subscription and nothing to unlock.
about.small.title: Runs on a small computer
about.small.body: Glazelab is small and efficient enough to run on a Raspberry Pi-class computer with an SSD, without problems.

terms.section.profilePicture.title: Your profile picture
terms.section.profilePicture.body: You can add a profile picture to your account. Every registered user with a confirmed email address can see it, for example in club member lists, in buddy lists and requests, and next to the combinations you have published. Guests who are not signed in cannot. It may show you or anything else you have the rights to. It must not show another person, and it must not be unlawful or harmful. Other users can report a profile picture. The site admins then see the report, the reporting user's display name and the reason given, and they may remove the picture. When you replace or remove your picture, it is no longer shown, and it is deleted at once unless it has been reported. Devices that have already loaded it may keep a copy in their browser cache for up to a week. A reported picture is kept so that the site admins can look into the report and act on it. Only they can see it. It is kept until the report is closed and for up to 90 days after that, even if you replace or remove it in the meantime. When the site admins remove a picture, Glazelab keeps a fingerprint of it with no time limit: values calculated from the image, not the image itself. With it, no account can upload the same picture again, or a copy of it that is only slightly changed. When the site admins remove an account after violations (see “Your account and contact”), they may block its reported pictures in the same way. Deleted pictures may remain in the server's backups for up to 7 days. When your account is deleted, by you or by the site admins, your pictures and every copy kept for a report are deleted at once, and so are the reasons given in reports about them. Only the reports' status and dates remain, and the fingerprint of a blocked picture stays so that it remains blocked.

terms.section.diagnostics.title: Error reports
terms.section.diagnostics.body: Error reports are off unless you turn them on, when you sign up or later on the Account page. Your choice applies on every device where you are signed in to your account. While they are on, the app sends Glazelab a short report when something goes wrong. A report contains the kind of problem (an error or a warning), its technical message and where in the app's code it happened; the app version; the name of the page (never its web address); when and how often it happened; and facts about your device at that moment: browser and operating system with their versions, screen and window size, pixel density, whether you use touch or a mouse, language, time zone, whether the app is installed and online, the connection type and memory size where the browser reports them, the state of the app's offline support, and your reduced-motion and light or dark setting. Now and then a technical message can contain a piece of what the page showed, such as a glaze name. Before a report is stored, anything that looks like an email address, a password, a link token or the part of a web address after a ? or # is removed. A report is linked to your account only by an internal ID. No email address, name or IP address is stored with it. Only the site admins see reports, and only to find and fix problems in the app. Reports are never shared or used for anything else. They are deleted after 30 days. If you turn error reports off on the Account page, they stop at once and the reports already stored for your account are deleted. Deleting your account deletes them too. Guests and signed-out visitors never send reports. Reports that have not been sent yet stay only in the app's memory, never in your device's storage.

users.body: All accounts by display name. For each account the list shows its name, its email address, whether it is active or still waiting for its email confirmation, and whether it is a site admin; it never shows passwords or anything else an account keeps.

admin.users.about: All accounts by name, with their status and whether they are site admins.
studio.recovery.title: Restore unfinished combination?
studio.recovery.body: An unfinished combination is saved on this device. Restore it to continue, or discard it. Restoring does not send anything; press Save when you are ready.
studio.recovery.failed: Your browser could not keep a recovery copy. Save your work before closing this page.

account.feed.title: Activity
account.feed.intro: The activity page and its badge show what your glaze buddies and the members of your clubs add, as far as you can see it anyway. It applies on every device where you are signed in.
account.feed.buddies: Show what my glaze buddies add
account.feed.clubs: Show what is added in my clubs

feedback.title: Send feedback
feedback.intro: Tell us what works, what is missing or what went wrong.
feedback.whatIsSent: Your text, photos and name go to the site admins only. Feedback is deleted 90 days after it was handled, or with your account.
feedback.offline: You are offline. Sending needs a connection; your feedback stays here.
feedback.problem.tooLong: Feedback can be at most 2000 characters.
feedback.problem.unreadable: This device cannot read that photo.
notices.feedbackSent: Thank you! Your feedback was sent.
notices.feedbackPhotoDropped: The feedback form closed before a photo was ready, so it was not added. Open the form and add it again.
admin.feedback.about: What signed-in users sent from the app, with photos; mark it done or delete it.
feedbackAdmin.title: Feedback
feedbackAdmin.body: Newest first. Feedback marked as done is deleted after {days} days; deleting removes it and its photos at once.
feedbackAdmin.adminOnly: Only site admins can read feedback.
feedbackAdmin.offline: You are offline. The feedback list needs a connection.
feedbackAdmin.delete.title: Delete this feedback?
feedbackAdmin.delete.body: The feedback from {name} is deleted at once, with its photos. This cannot be undone.
terms.section.diagnostics.feedback: Feedback you send from the app is read only by the site admins, with your name, any photos you add and, unless you untick it, the page name, app version, language and device type; it is deleted 90 days after it was marked as done, and at once when you delete your account.
errors.feedbackTooLong: Feedback can be at most 2000 characters.
errors.nameInvalid: Use visible characters in the name, without control or formatting characters.
errors.requestTooLarge: This is too much data to send at once.
errors.textControlCharacters: Remove control characters from the text.
account.page.feedback.body: Something not working, missing or great? Tell the site admins; you can add photos or screenshots.
studio.photos.title: Photos (optional)
studio.photos.hint: Test tiles or finished pieces. They upload once the combination is published or saved.
studio.photos.offline: You are offline. Photos need a connection, so this save cannot wait: keep this page open until you are back online, or remove the photos to save later.
studio.photos.failed: The combination is saved. Try the photos that did not upload again, or choose Done to open it without them.
studio.photos.dropped: You left Studio before every photo was uploaded. The combination is saved: add the missing photos from its page.
studio.photos.notKept: {count, plural, one {You had # photo attached. Photos are not kept on this device: add it again.} other {You had # photos attached. Photos are not kept on this device: add them again.}}
studio.leave.photosBody: The combination is saved anyway, but photos not yet uploaded are dropped. You can add them later from its page.
